findings.title: Unrelated change: background cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker interval for the whole cleanup service is changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This is not mentioned in the PR description and has nothing to do with the annotation deadlock fix. It makes every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, annotations) run ten times as often on every instance, adding DB load. It looks like a leftover debugging change and should be reverted unless it is intentional and documented.

findings.title: Routine per-batch progress is logged at Error level, including full ID lists
findings.body: Every batch of the time-based cleanup logs at Error level ("Annotations to clean by time", with the full "ids" slice and the SQL "cond"), and then logs again at Error level after deletion (line 536). The same happens for the count-based cleanup (lines 554, 556) and for orphaned tags (lines 576, 579). A healthy cleanup run therefore emits error-level logs for every batch, and each line can contain up to batch-size IDs. This floods logs and triggers error alerts on success. Also, the 'err' field in these calls is always nil at that point. These should be Debug-level and should not include the ID list.

findings.title: Quadratic string building when inlining IDs for SQLite
findings.body: For SQLite with batch sizes above 999, the IDs are concatenated with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v). Each iteration copies the whole accumulated string, so building a 32767-element list is O(n^2) work and allocation on every batch. Use strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt into a byte slice.

findings.title: Test with 40003 annotations is slow and is the only coverage for the large-batch SQLite path
findings.body: The new case inserts 40003 annotations and 80006 tags through InsertMulti on every run, and it is the only test that exercises the inlined-ID SQLite branch in deleteByIDs. This makes the integration suite noticeably slower. Also, the new integration tests are now skipped under testing.Short(), so the cleanup logic has no unit-level coverage in short runs. Consider a smaller test that still crosses the 999 threshold, or a unit test for deleteByIDs that does not need the DB.

findings.title: Test cleanup does not clear annotation_tag rows
findings.body: TestIntegrationOldAnnotationsAreDeletedFirst removes only the annotation table in its t.Cleanup, while the other test in this file removes both annotation and annotation_tag. Leftover tag rows can leak into other tests in the package that count annotation_tag, making results depend on test order.
